output.headline: Awards Deco Tech Systems $101,854 to install about 20 new security cameras at Lincoln Elementary
output.summary: The board is choosing Deco Tech Systems as the lowest responsive, responsible bidder and rejecting all other bids. The company will install about 20 new cameras, fix one existing camera, supply about 3 spare cameras and replace the recording server at Lincoln Elementary School. The amount includes a $9,000 contingency allowance, and work is expected to run from August 27 to November 25, 2026.

output.headline: Pays Consolidated Engineering Laboratories up to $7,656 for more soil testing at Garfield Elementary
output.summary: The district is hiring Consolidated Engineering Laboratories for further geotechnical (soil and ground) consultation on the new Garfield Elementary School construction project. The work includes engineer meetings and analysis and compaction testing of backfill. The $7,656 limit includes a $696 contingency fee for additional services, and the work lasts for the duration of the project.

output.headline: Adds $823 for inspection services on the Markham Elementary boys' restroom renovation
output.summary: This amendment gives King Construction Inspection, Inc. additional inspection work on the Markham Elementary School boys' toilet room renovation. It adds $823 and raises the contract's not-to-exceed amount from $7,832 to $8,655. All other terms stay the same.

output.headline: Ratifies a no-cost research partnership with Stanford to support teachers' math language practices
output.summary: The board is approving a no-cost services agreement with Stanford Graduate School of Education. Researchers will work with OUSD teachers on co-planning to support multilingual learners' math talk, share de-identified results and offer open-source tools. A data sharing agreement (DSA) sets rules for sharing and protecting student data. Both run January 30 through December 31, 2026, at no cost to the district.

vendor.name: Board of Trustees of Stanford University (Stanford Graduate School of Education)

output.headline: Ratifies up to $42,000 for Smartcat translation software and services for one year
output.summary: The board is approving after the fact an agreement with Smartcat Platform, Inc. for subscription and translation services, handled through the Special Education Department. The term is July 14, 2026 through July 13, 2027, for up to $42,000.

output.headline: Hires Invo Healthcare for special education mental health staff, up to $70,000 through 2029
output.sourceIssueCandidate: The stated $70,000 limit appears small for 15 or more full-time staff over nearly three years, so the amount may be misprinted or may cover only part of the cost.
output.summary: Invo Healthcare Associates would provide seven full-time mental health clinicians, seven behavioral health technicians, a therapeutic behavior support provider and a program supervisor. They would deliver counseling required by students' Individualized Education Programs (IEPs). A data sharing agreement covers student data. The term runs August 5, 2026 through June 30, 2029, for up to $70,000.

output.headline: Pays YouthBeat up to $180,000 for after-school music and digital arts at 11 schools
output.summary: YouthBeat will run after-school music and digital arts classes, up to two days a week, with up to 20 students per class. Up to 200 students would get 1,200 hours of free instruction across 11 school sites. The term is August 3, 2026 through June 30, 2027.

output.headline: Adds $43,077 to Deco Tech's security camera and door entry maintenance contract, now $563,927
output.summary: This change order adds general maintenance work so security cameras and door entry systems at various district sites keep being serviced. It raises the contract price from $520,850 to $563,927. All other terms stay the same.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $80,000 for East Bay Art Therapy after-school group therapy at four schools
output.summary: The board is approving after the fact an agreement with East Bay Art Therapy to provide after-school, arts-based group therapy at four school sites, at least one day a week. Groups serve up to 10 students per session, reaching up to 85 students for 120 hours of free art therapy. The term is August 3, 2026 through June 30, 2027.

output.headline: Adds $11,796.39 and 23 days to the Markham Elementary boys' restroom renovation contract
output.summary: This change order pays Next Generation of Builders for extra work on the Markham Elementary School boys' toilet renovation: concrete replacement after unforeseen conditions, a toilet flange repair, added ceiling conduit supports and an upgraded light fixture. It raises the contract price from $238,475 to $250,271.39 and extends the end date from July 31 to August 21, 2026.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $100,000 for Destiny Arts Center visual and performing arts classes at five schools
output.summary: The board is approving after the fact an agreement with Destiny Arts Center for visual and performing arts classes at five school sites. Classes of up to 20 students meet twice a week over 30 weeks, serving about 150 students with 1,200 hours of instruction. The term is August 3, 2026 through June 30, 2027.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $50,000 for CloudBase to upgrade the Summer Learning timekeeping and payroll platform
output.summary: The board is approving after the fact a contract with CloudBase Services to improve the district's existing Summer Learning platform. The upgrades cover timekeeping, payroll preparation, reporting and workflow automation, based on experience from the 2026 Summer Learning Program. The term is August 1 through September 30, 2026.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $75,000 for Dimensions Dance Theatre out-of-school dance classes at three schools
output.summary: The board is approving after the fact an agreement with Dimensions Dance Theatre to teach cultural dance styles of the African Diaspora and world cultures. Classes run up to 2 days a week with up to 20 students per class over 30 weeks, for 720 hours. The term is August 3, 2026 through June 30, 2027.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $53,060 for Scientific Adventures for Girls after-school STEM at two elementary schools
output.summary: The board is approving after the fact an agreement with Scientific Adventures for Girls for weekly after-school science, technology, engineering and math sessions. Up to 180 elementary school girls at two schools take part over 24 weeks. The term is September 1, 2026 through May 31, 2027.

output.headline: Pays HERO up to $90,000 to run a structured recess program at Laurel Elementary
output.summary: HERO will run a structured recess program at Laurel Elementary School with active supervision and organized games, aimed at student leadership and fewer conflicts. It also offers the Young HERO Program for upper-grade students, with monthly leadership workshops. The term is August 10, 2026 through June 25, 2027.

output.headline: Pays East Bay Agency for Children up to $132,000 for mental health support at Rudsdale High
output.summary: East Bay Agency for Children will provide 40 hours a week of clinical mental health support to students at Rudsdale Continuation High School. It will also offer staff training classes and 4.5 hours of consultation. The term is July 13, 2026 through June 30, 2027.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $105,000 for Public Profit to evaluate the district's 84 after-school programs
output.summary: The board is approving after the fact a contract with Public Profit to evaluate OUSD's 84 Expanded Learning Programs. The firm will survey students and families, hold four meetings with 130 site coordinators and agency directors, and give each school a program profile. The term is July 15, 2026 through June 30, 2027.

output.headline: Cuts $2.02M from Syserco's CAL Shape ventilation contract, lowering it to $7.82M
output.summary: This change order reduces the Syserco Energy Solutions design-build contract by a net $2,021,327.02, lowering it from $9,837,080.68 to $7,815,753.66. Most of the cut is a $2,033,894.75 reduction in ventilation work across 78 sites to match the work actually completed. Small additions for contingency repairs and second-shift work to install CO2 sensors in active classrooms partly offset it.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $32,000 for a contractor to run weekly food bank distribution at Rudsdale High
output.summary: The board is approving after the fact an agreement with an individual contractor to coordinate weekly food bank pickups and distribution at Rudsdale Continuation High School. About 2,500 pounds of fresh and non-perishable food would be distributed weekly, plus 4 special event distributions. The term is August 1, 2026 through May 28, 2027.

output.headline: Ratifies $5,000 for Cantare Con Vivo to teach music classes at La Escuelita Elementary
output.summary: The board is approving after the fact an agreement with Cantare Con Vivo for music classes at La Escuelita Elementary School. The classes teach music fundamentals, follow a standards-based curriculum, and end with a performance showcase for the school community. The term is August 11, 2026 through May 27, 2027, for up to $5,000.

output.headline: Pays Soccer Without Borders up to $48,300 for soccer and wellness support at Rudsdale Continuation High
output.summary: Soccer Without Borders will serve 60 students at Rudsdale Continuation High School through weekly practices, coaching, mentorship and league play. The money also covers uniforms, equipment, league fees and transportation support. The agreement runs from August 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027, and the work period began before this vote.

output.headline: Ratifies a no-cost agreement for Fred Finch to offer therapy services at Garfield Elementary
output.summary: The board is approving after the fact a no-cost agreement with Fred Finch Youth & Family Services to provide student therapy at Garfield Elementary School. Services include individual, group and family therapy, crisis intervention, workshops and psychoeducation. The term is August 10, 2026 through May 31, 2027.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $5,000 for an individual contractor to provide computer support at Edna Brewer Middle
output.summary: The board is approving after the fact an agreement with an individual contractor for technical support for Windows and Mac computers at Edna Brewer Middle School. The work includes maintaining the school network and setting up printing, including for Chromebooks. The term is August 1 through September 15, 2026.

output.headline: Ratifies $7,974 for Vik Staffing to run on-site support at the New Teacher Institute
output.summary: The board is approving after the fact an agreement with Vik Staffing for on-site event help at the New Teacher Institute. The help includes breakfast and lunch setup, bussing and general event assistance for new teachers, staff and facilitators. The work covered July 27 to July 31, 2026, for up to $7,974.

output.headline: Pays Shred Works up to $12,000 to shred confidential documents at district offices
output.summary: Shred Works of Los Angeles will shred confidential documents at the district's central offices. The agreement runs from August 7, 2026 through May 31, 2027, and the work period began before this vote.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $11,680 for Cooperative Personnel Services to study how district jobs are classified
output.summary: The board is approving after the fact a contract with Cooperative Personnel Services to conduct job classification studies for district positions. The firm will review job questionnaires, interview employees and supervisors, and recommend updates or new job specifications. The term is July 22, 2026 through June 30, 2027.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $12,000 for a consultant to build college partnerships for new teacher recruitment
output.summary: The board is approving after the fact a contract with William L. Winston, Education Consulting LLC to set up partnerships with colleges and universities. The consultant will draft and negotiate memorandums of understanding (written partnership agreements) to support recruiting new teachers. The term is August 10, 2026 through June 30, 2027.

vendor.name: William L. Winston, Education Consulting LLC

output.headline: Ratifies up to $8,000 for Urban Leader Coaching to coach Allendale Elementary leaders on reading instruction
output.summary: The board is approving after the fact an agreement with Urban Leader Coaching, LLC to coach the principal and the Teacher on Special Assignment at Allendale Elementary School. Virtual 60-minute sessions will cover data review and strategies for coaching teachers in reading instruction. The term is August 17, 2026 through April 30, 2027.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $58,598 for Sobrato Early Academic Language to lead early learning training sessions
output.summary: The board is approving after the fact an agreement with Sobrato Early Academic Language (SEAL). Up to two presenters will deliver four of the Designs for Change Four-Day Early Learning Series for the Early Childhood Development Department. The term is August 17, 2026 through June 30, 2027.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $23,102 for Wellness Together counseling support at Urban Promise Academy
output.summary: The board is approving after the fact an agreement with Wellness Together to provide counseling support at Urban Promise Academy. Services include individual and group counseling, family engagement sessions, classroom presentations and community referrals. The term is August 10, 2026 through May 31, 2027.

output.headline: Accepts free science teaching support for all elementary schools from Community Resources for Science
output.summary: Community Resources For Science of Berkeley will give all OUSD elementary schools free help with science teaching. This includes leading science lessons in classrooms, offering teacher training and resources, and providing on-call planning help. The agreement runs from September 10, 2026 through May 30, 2027 and costs the district nothing.

output.headline: Accepts free poetry and literature workshops from Bay Area Creative at Franklin Elementary
output.summary: Bay Area Creative will run poetry and literature workshops for students at Franklin Elementary School. The workshops build vocabulary, awareness of sounds in words, and reading fluency. The agreement runs from August 17, 2026 through May 21, 2027 at no cost to the district, and the work period began before this vote.

output.headline: Pays Oakland Public Education Fund up to $255,000 to hire tobacco and drug prevention coaches
output.summary: Oakland Public Education Fund will hire Tobacco Use Prevention Education (TUPE) coaches to work one-on-one with students and lead small drug intervention groups. Each coach handles up to 10 students per school and also does outreach and classroom presentations. The agreement runs from August 10, 2026 through June 30, 2027, and the work period began before this vote.

output.headline: Accepts free after-school drop-in program from Trybe and a data sharing agreement for student information
output.summary: Trybe, Inc. will run a free after-school drop-in program at San Antonio Park Courts with college and career mentoring and peer activities. Students come from several schools, mainly Roosevelt Middle, Garfield Elementary and Oakland High. A separate data sharing agreement sets rules for the district sharing student data with Trybe and for Trybe protecting it. Both run August 13, 2026 through August 12, 2027 at no cost, and the work period began before this vote.

output.headline: Approves Personnel Report No. 2627-0001 from the Talent/Human Resources Department
output.summary: This is the first personnel report of the 2026-27 school year from the Talent/Human Resources Department. The official text does not list the individual personnel actions or any dollar amounts.

output.headline: Pays a science assistant up to $34,200 to support K-5 teachers at Chabot Elementary
output.summary: A contractor will work as a science assistant at Chabot Elementary School, helping K-5 teachers set up experiments and deliver hands-on lessons. The assistant also organizes science supplies and the school Science Fair. The agreement runs from August 5, 2026 through June 30, 2027, and the work period began before this vote.

output.headline: Approves a no-cost agreement with Smith College to place social work graduate students in district schools
output.summary: This memorandum of understanding (a written partnership agreement) sets up a practicum program for Smith College School for Social Work graduate students in pupil personnel services fields. It runs July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2031 and costs the district nothing. Some non-employee interns may receive stipends paid from nonprofit grants to the district, such as from the Ed Fund.

output.headline: Pays The Finer Print up to $5,500 for design work on the district's Crisis Response Manual
output.summary: The Finer Print of Berkeley will provide up to 35 hours of graphic design and layout for an updated district Crisis Response Manual. The update reflects current practices, including police-free responses to student mental health crises. The work period was July 15 through August 1, 2026, which was before this vote.

output.headline: Accepts free literacy support from Accelerating Literacy Leadership Institute and a student data agreement
output.summary: Accelerating Literacy Leadership Institute will provide literacy support to schools and central district teams at no cost. A separate data sharing agreement sets rules for the district sharing student data with the group and for the group protecting it. Both run from August 13, 2026 through August 13, 2027, and the work period began before this vote.

output.headline: Accepts a free student internship and career training program from Genesys Works Bay Area through 2029
output.summary: Genesys Works Bay Area will offer an internship and training program to eligible high school students in underserved communities, with skills training and work experience. The agreement runs from April 30, 2026 through January 1, 2029 at no cost to the district, and it began before this vote.

output.headline: Pays HERO up to $45,000 for recess programs and student leaders at Think College Now Elementary
output.summary: HERO will run structured activities during recess and lunch recess at Think College Now Elementary School. It will also train student leaders to reduce conflicts and build a stronger sense of belonging. The agreement runs from August 10, 2026 through May 27, 2027, and the work period began before this vote.

output.headline: Pays a consultant up to $119,000 to coordinate early childhood mental health services
output.summary: A consultant will coordinate mental health services across 17 OUSD Child Development Centers. The work includes consulting on children's social-emotional needs, coaching and training educators, running parent workshops, and connecting families to outside services. The agreement runs from August 24, 2026 through June 30, 2027.

output.headline: Pays Ball for Life Oakland up to $35,000 for a physical education and recess program at Reach Academy
output.summary: Ball for Life Oakland LLC will run a structured physical education and recess program at Reach Academy. It will provide active supervision and organized games that promote teamwork and a safe, inclusive playground. The agreement runs from August 10, 2026 through May 27, 2027, and the work period began before this vote.

output.headline: Accepts a free structured recess program from HERO at Cleveland Elementary
output.summary: HERO will run a structured recess program at Cleveland Elementary School to increase student engagement, reduce conflicts and create a safe, inclusive playground. The agreement runs from August 10, 2026 through May 27, 2027 at no cost to the district, and the work period began before this vote.

output.headline: Pays HERO up to $45,000 for a recess and leadership program at Horace Mann Elementary
output.summary: HERO will run a structured recess program at Horace Mann Elementary School, guiding students in conflict resolution and teamwork. Upper grade students also get the Young HERO Program, a daily leadership activity. The agreement runs from August 10, 2026 through May 27, 2027, and the work period began before this vote.

output.headline: Pays HERO up to $58,800 for a recess and leadership program at Hoover Elementary
output.summary: HERO will run a structured recess program at Hoover Elementary School, plus the Young HERO Program, a daily leadership activity for upper grade students. It also offers monthly leadership workshops and cooperative games to build problem-solving skills. The agreement runs from August 10, 2026 through May 27, 2027, and the work period began before this vote.

output.headline: Pays East Bay Agency for Children up to $60,000 for a Spanish-speaking counselor at Greenleaf Elementary
output.summary: East Bay Agency for Children will provide a bilingual Spanish mental health provider at Greenleaf Elementary School. The provider will meet one-on-one each week with a caseload of 10 to 15 children. The agreement runs from August 24, 2026 through May 27, 2027.

output.headline: Pays Connected Minds Consulting Group up to $10,000 for a full-day training for early childhood educators
output.summary: Connected Minds Consulting Group will lead a full-day professional learning institute for early childhood educators. It includes a keynote speech and two learning sessions on belonging, anti-bias education, trauma-responsive practice and family partnerships. The agreement runs from August 17, 2026 through June 30, 2027, and the work period began before this vote.

output.headline: Pays Navalta Media up to $114,000 for strategic communications and media relations support
output.summary: Navalta Media of Fairfield will provide strategic communications, media relations, reputation management and executive communications support to the district. The agreement runs from July 22, 2026 through May 22, 2027, and the work period began before this vote.

output.headline: Declares district vehicles surplus and authorizes their disposal under Resolution 2627-0016
output.summary: The board is asked to approve a resolution declaring certain district vehicles obsolete and surplus. The resolution also authorizes the district to dispose of them. The text lists no dollar amounts.

output.headline: Updates the dental plan agreement with Self-Insured Schools of California to add a data-sharing rule
output.summary: The district's dental plan administration agreement with Self Insured Schools of California (SISC III) gets a new section on outside companies. The district cannot contract with any third party that handles electronic eligibility data without SISC III's prior approval and a signed business associate agreement. The change takes effect July 1, 2026, and all other terms stay the same.

output.headline: Ratifies the minutes of the August 24, 2026 special Board of Education meeting
output.summary: The board is asked to approve the written minutes of its Special Meeting held on August 24, 2026. Staff prepared the minutes shortly after the meeting.

output.headline: Ratifies the minutes of the August 26, 2026 regular Board of Education meeting
output.summary: The board is asked to approve the written minutes of its Regular Meeting held on August 26, 2026. Staff prepared the minutes shortly after the meeting.
